accuracy.evidence: Uses the GCSE 2,8,8 model for Z ≤ 20 and says so; notes that the third shell can hold 18 in fuller models; helium and full outer shells placed in group 0; every configuration in items and challenge (F, Al, S, Ca, Mg, Ar, B, K) checked.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets: third electron joins shell 1, shell 3 fills to 18 before shell 4, group read from number of shells, and adding extra electrons (ion) when asked for a neutral atom.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is about fill order: free placement with an 'unstable: shell n has room' warning and a live mini periodic table linking shells to period and outer electrons to group; nothing here is a nucleus builder.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover the fill order from the warning and the shell caps, then see group/period light up on the table when each atom is complete.

predictions.evidence: 'Shell 1 again, it is closest', 'It has 7 shells' and 'Shell 3: it can take up to 18' are each tempting and each is disproved by the build.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Distinct messages for too few electrons, too many (negative ion), an outer shell used while an inner one has room, and the 2-8-8 limit.

readability.evidence: Validator readability passes; kid text uses one idea per sentence with the sodium 2,8,1 worked example.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases; each paragraph gives a rule, a worked configuration or a named slip.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots: atom above a centred 8x4 table, symbol labels readable, shell buttons wrap and stay reachable, nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Add/remove buttons for every shell and Z −/+ as alternatives to tapping rings; canvas aria-label states configuration, warning, group and period live; axe clean.

sources: AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462 spec 4.1.1.7 Electronic structure
